extracted.intended_audience: Investigators preparing NIH/NCI grant applications (e.g., R01 applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and organizing NIH (SF 424 / PHS398) grant applications, covering planning, required sections (Project Summary, Research Plan: Specific Aims, Significance, Innovation, Approach), budget, assurances, human subjects, animals, resources, and overall application presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarize with SF 424 and PHS398 application guides
rubrics_metrics.description: Before you begin writing your grant application, familiarize yourself with the new NIH SF 424 Application Guide for electronic applications and all the requirements and certifications. See NIH Forms and Applications for other types of required forms and applications, including the PHS 398 application for multi-component applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know which application instructions apply (SF 424 vs PHS398) and follow them exactly; these guides determine required forms, certifications, and formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission systems and registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission of electronic applications to NIH involves interaction between Grants.gov and the NIH eRA Commons. Individual investigators do not need to register with Grants.gov, but you must be a registered Commons user to submit an application or be included as a Senior/Key Person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure required institutional and PI registrations are completed well before the deadline; consult Electronic Submission guidance for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to an appropriate Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA)
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications must be submitted in response to a Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA). Responding to an FOA ensures the correct application package is used and enables NIH to receive the application from Grants.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find Parent FOAs or RFAs/PAs as appropriate; read the FOA carefully to ensure your project is responsive and you use the correct package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe FOA-specific receipt dates and standard due dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadlines depend on grant mechanism and FOA. For new R01s use Feb 5, Jun 5, Oct 5; renewals/resubmissions use Mar 5, Jul 5, Nov 5. FOAs with special receipt dates may differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always check the FOA for the receipt date and account for institutional deadlines, equipment/personnel contingencies, and system registration lead time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow sufficient time for review cycle and aim for highest quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The review and selection process takes 8–10 months. Submit your very best application because reviewers expect time and thought to have been taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan early; incomplete or rushed applications are likely to be less competitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission policy and responding to reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: For new investigators there is an opportunity for resubmission in the next review round when there are only minor concerns. When submitting a revised application, answer all reviewer concerns mentioned in the earlier Summary Statement. Substantial scientific changes must be described in the Introduction and marked in the text by bracketing, indenting, or change of typography. Only one resubmission is allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond comprehensively and visibly to reviewer critiques; mark changes clearly; plan resubmission carefully since only one is allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek institutional assistance and examples of successful applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If possible, find someone in your institution to assist you in understanding and completing the application. Ask colleagues for copies of successful NIH grant applications to get a concrete idea of what each section should include.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use experienced colleagues and institutional grants offices; review exemplars to align expectations with reviewers'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete applications returned without review
rubrics_metrics.description: Incomplete applications are returned without review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the checklists and application instructions to ensure completeness before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set internal deadlines and allow contingency time
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish deadlines for preparation, particularly when collaborating investigators are involved. Be aware of institutional deadlines that could delay your application. Allow time for equipment failures, personnel shortages, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate contributors early and build slack into the schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish preliminary data when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish the papers; you can only cite published or accepted-for-publication papers. With new page limitations, preliminary data should be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where feasible, publish supporting preliminary results to cite as evidence of feasibility and productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know NIH peer review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Become familiar with the NIH peer review criteria; reviewers will use them to rate your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and write the application to address standard review criteria (e.g., Significance, Innovation, Approach, Investigators, Environment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple principal investigators appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: If several people have major contributions to the research project, consider the option for multiple Principal Investigators (PIs). A Leadership Plan is required and New Investigator policies do not apply unless all PIs are New Investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear leadership plan; understand policy implications for New Investigator status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain objective external critiques
rubrics_metrics.description: If possible, have objective experts (e.g., successful grantees, an institutional panel) review your application. Friends or close associates are rarely as critical as study section reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use impartial reviewers who will critically evaluate significance, rigor, and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact program representatives for advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Request technical assistance from the funding agency or your institution. Talk to the program representative who will manage the grant for advice on scientific and technical issues, grant mechanisms, and information on special initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage program staff early with specific questions about fit and priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate agency research priorities and FOAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate any special research priorities of funding agencies. Search the NIH Guide for Grants and Contracts for current FOAs and ascertain from the program representative whether your project falls within scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align your proposal to agency priorities where appropriate; explicit responsiveness can improve competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional conduct with reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not insult the reviewers. If you differ in opinion try to courteously convince the reviewers of your point-of-views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain professionalism in responses and discussions; avoid adversarial tone in rebuttals and revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract: succinct and comprehensive
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Summary/Abstract should describe succinctly every major aspect of the proposed project and contain a statement of objectives and methods. Members of the Study Section who are not primary reviewers may rely heavily on the abstract to understand your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider significance and innovation; the abstract will be used beyond review (reports, dissemination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract length and formatting limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Project Summary must be no longer than 30 lines of text, and follow the required font and margin specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere strictly to the line, font, and margin limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract: public health relevance and plain language
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a component on the relevance of research to public health using plain language understandable by a general, lay audience. The Project Summary should not contain proprietary confidential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write a clear lay summary for broader audiences; avoid confidential/proprietary details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract content elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract should include: a brief background of the project; specific aims, objectives, or hypotheses; expected results; and description of how your results will affect other research areas; significance and relevance to public health; unique features and innovation; methodology (action steps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be complete but brief; use all allotted space; avoid describing past accomplishments and use of the first person; write the abstract last so it reflects the entire application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy alignment with review criteria (Significance, Innovation, Approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH restructured applications so Research Strategy/Plan is organized into Significance, Innovation, and Approach to align with review criteria; assessment of this plan largely determines funding recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address each review criterion clearly; for multiple Specific Aims you may address S/I/A per aim or collectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy: core content questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Research Strategy should answer: What do you intend to do? Why is this worth doing (significance; innovation)? What has been done already and what will this add? What have you done to establish feasibility? How will the research be accomplished (who, what, when, where, why)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the narrative to answer these explicitly; use appropriate references to situate the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan internal consistency and navigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure all sections are internally consistent and dovetail with each other. Use a numbering system and make sections easy to find. Lead the reviewers through your research plan. One person should revise and edit the final draft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure coherence among aims, approach, budget, and timelines; avoid contradictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims: concise goals and expected outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific Aims should describe concisely and realistically the goals of the proposed research and summarize expected outcomes, including impact on the research fields involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended length is one page; begin with a brief narrative of long-term goals/hypothesis followed by a numbered list of aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims: content requirements and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Content should cover specific objectives and hypotheses to be tested; broad, long-term goals; summarize expected outcomes; describe impact on the research field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims should be clearly stated, testable, supported by citations/preliminary data; each aim ideally one sentence, most successful applications have 2–4 aims, and aims should be related and not overly ambitious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance section: explain importance and contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance should explain the importance of the problem or critical barrier and how the project will improve scientific knowledge, technical capability, and/or clinical practice; describe how concepts/methods/technologies will be changed if aims are achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended length ~1–2 pages; include state of existing knowledge with citations, gaps addressed, rationale, potential contribution, public health implications, and attainable timeframes for aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation section: demonstrate paradigm-shifting aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the application challenges or seeks to shift current research/clinical practice paradigms; describe novel theoretical concepts, approaches/methodologies, instrumentation, interventions, or improvements and advantages over existing methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended length 1/2–1 page; explain why concepts/methods are novel, focus on innovation in study design and outcomes, and summarize novel preliminary findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach section: detailed research design and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach should describe how the research will be carried out and is crucial to favorable review. Include PI's preliminary studies, overview of experimental design, methods and analyses to accomplish aims, discussion of potential difficulties and limitations and how they will be overcome, expected results and alternative approaches, projected timetable, feasibility strategies for early-stage projects, and description of data collection/analysis/interpretation and any new methodology and why it is an improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximum recommended length for Approach is 9–10 pages (R01 example). Number sections to correspond to Specific Aims; integrate or place preliminary data appropriately; avoid excessive experimental detail by citing publications (preferably your own); explain not only how but why methods were chosen; add experienced co-investigators for complex technologies; document collaborations with letters; point out hazardous procedures and precautions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss potential difficulties and alternative strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a discussion of potential difficulties and limitations and how these will be overcome or mitigated, and describe alternative approaches if unexpected results are found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate forethought and contingency planning; this strengthens reviewers' confidence in the project's feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timetable/work plan and feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a projected sequence or timetable (work plan) and, if the project is early stage, describe strategies to establish feasibility and manage high-risk aspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include timeframes for each Specific Aim and show objectives are attainable within the stated period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection, analysis, interpretation, and resource sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a detailed discussion of the way in which results will be collected, analyzed, and interpreted and describe resource sharing plans as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about analytic methods, statistical approaches, and plans for sharing data, organisms, or GWAS data where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document collaborations and availability of materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Document proposed collaborations and offers of materials or reagents of restricted availability with letters from individuals involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include signed letters of collaboration that specify the nature and extent of support or materials to be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and justification: present and justify expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: The budget and justification present and justify all expenses required to achieve project aims. For multi-institutional applications there must be a separate budget for each subcontractor or consortium member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow special forms and instructions; modular budgets apply for direct costs ≤ $250,000/year; consult guidelines for modular vs non-modular requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget details: personnel, consultants, equipment, supplies, travel
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget content should cover personnel, consultants, equipment, supplies, travel, and other expenses (e.g., animal maintenance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide brief descriptions of duties, number of person months requested, identify specific individuals when possible, justify equipment (especially major items), breakout supply costs for non-modular budgets, and explain year-to-year fluctuations consistent with the research plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget realism and institutional approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Be realistic — both over-padding and deliberate under-budgeting are viewed negatively. The budget must be approved by the grantee institution business office before they can sign the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check current salary limitations with your office of sponsored programs; ensure indirect cost rates are correct and get institutional sign-off before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular vs non-modular budget handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Modular budgets are applicable to research grant applications requesting $250,000 or less per year in direct costs and are simplified; detailed categorical information is not submitted. For non-modular budgets, provide detailed justification for equipment and break out supply costs into major categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow modular instructions when eligible; for non-modular, prepare detailed, well-justified categorical budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurances and regulatory compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assurances ensure the applicant organization will comply with relevant Federal laws and guidelines. Assurances cover Human Subjects Research; Transplantation of Human Fetal Tissue; Human Embryonic Stem Cells; Inclusion Policies for Women, Minorities, Children; Vertebrate Animals; Debarments; Drug-Free Workplace; Lobbying; Non-Delinquency of Federal Debt; Research Misconduct; Civil Rights; Handicapped Individuals; Sex and Age Discrimination; Recombinant DNA; Financial Conflict of Interest; Smoke-Free Workplace; Prohibited Research; Select Agent Research; and Principal Investigator Assurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the special assurance forms early; coordinate with institutional compliance offices as different institutions may have additional procedures and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects protections and required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a complete description of proposed involvement of human subjects as it relates to the Research Plan. If exempt, provide sufficient detail to determine appropriateness. Provide enough information for reviewers to determine that the proposed research meets: (1) DHHS regulations (45 CFR Part 46); (2) NIH/NCI Data and Safety Monitoring policies; (3) ClinicalTrials.gov requirements, if applicable; (4) NIH inclusion policies for women, minorities, and children; and (5) NIH policy on reporting race and ethnicity data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inclusion of women/minorities is involved, complete the Targeted/Planned Enrollment Table and justify any limited representation; failure to address these issues may bar funding until resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate animal use considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a complete description of proposed use of vertebrate animals as it relates to the Research Plan. Five points must be addressed (see PHS 398 or SF 424 instructions). Be thorough in addressing these areas; failure to do so will delay award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address humane treatment, justification, veterinary care, procedures to minimize pain/distress, and alternatives where applicable (consult application instructions for the five required points).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources and environment: describe institutional support
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the resources, facilities, and support available to the researcher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address all requirements of the research plan, justify reliance on external resources, ensure subcontractors/consortium members have capability to perform assigned tasks, ensure consistency between resources and budget, and include appropriate letters of collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall application presentation and style
rubrics_metrics.description: Observe application guidelines strictly: use basic English and avoid jargon, spell out acronyms upon first use, observe type size and page limitations strictly (do not use a small font), include only unpublished and essential graphs/tables, ensure complete citations (including NIHMS or PMCID numbers where required), include Resource Sharing Plans if appropriate, have an outside reader review for clarity and consistency, proofread aloud, and be consistent with terms, references, and form writing style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to formatting and style rules; clear, concise, error-free writing improves reviewer comprehension and application competitiveness.
